tax-filing-stage-1.title: The Starting Point
tax-filing-stage-1.description: One server runs the tax math, one database remembers the return

nodes.label: Filer Browser
nodes.explanation: The taxpayer's browser, where they answer interview questions and enter the numbers from their W-2

nodes.label: Tax App
nodes.explanation: A single server that runs the interview, calculates the return, and saves progress to the database

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: Stores each in-progress and filed return so a user can leave and come back without losing their work

tax-filing-stage-2.title: Engine and E-File
tax-filing-stage-2.description: Tax logic moves to a dedicated engine; filing happens through a queue

nodes.label: Filer Browser
nodes.explanation: The taxpayer's browser, now handling multi-state returns, itemized deductions, and business income

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.explanation: Handles logins, the interview, and saving progress, then hands the numbers to the calculation engine

nodes.label: Calc Engine
nodes.explanation: A dedicated engine where federal and each state's tax rules live as separate modules, so one state's change can't break another

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: Stores in-progress returns, filed returns, and the submission status of each filing

nodes.label: Filing Queue
nodes.explanation: Holds 'submit this return' jobs so the user gets an instant confirmation instead of waiting on the IRS

nodes.label: E-File Worker
nodes.explanation: Pulls jobs off the queue and submits each return to the IRS and state agencies, retrying when they're slow or down

nodes.label: IRS / States
nodes.explanation: Government e-file systems that accept or reject each return, often slowly and sometimes offline

tax-filing-stage-3.title: Deadline Night
tax-filing-stage-3.description: A load balancer fans out to many servers and engines, with a cache and read replica

nodes.label: Filer Browser
nodes.explanation: One of millions of taxpayers all trying to file before midnight on April 15

nodes.label: Load Balancer
nodes.explanation: Spreads incoming requests across many identical app servers and routes around any that crash under load

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.explanation: One of many identical app servers handling filers in parallel during the deadline rush

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.explanation: Another identical app server sharing the deadline-night load with the first

nodes.label: Calc Engine
nodes.explanation: The tax calculation engine, also scaled out so the heavy math runs in parallel across many machines

nodes.label: Rules Cache
nodes.explanation: Holds shared tax tables — federal brackets, state rate schedules, form definitions — in memory so engines don't reload them per return

nodes.label: Filing Queue
nodes.explanation: Buffers filing jobs so a midnight surge of submissions doesn't overwhelm the IRS or block users

nodes.label: Primary DB
nodes.explanation: Handles all writes — saving progress and recording filed returns — with locks that guarantee a return is filed exactly once

nodes.label: Read Replica
nodes.explanation: A synchronized copy that serves the constant reloads of in-progress returns, keeping that traffic off the primary

nodes.label: E-File Worker
nodes.explanation: Submits queued returns to the IRS and states, retrying as they allow, and emails the user when each is accepted

nodes.label: IRS / States
nodes.explanation: Government e-file systems that accept or reject each return, often slowly and sometimes offline
